label: First copy step (after <DEL>) in short L=3/4 sequences built from k/l/m/o/z/p then m/o/p then x/o/z
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.002% of steps). About 93% of activations fall on the step just after <DEL>, where the fed-back first token is input and original token 1 is output (recall_idx==1, prev_tok=<DEL>). It occurs almost only in short sequences (L=3: 35x lift, L=4: 5.6x) and almost only in all-letter sequences. It is selective for a narrow combination of tokens: first token in {k,l,m,o,z,(p)}, second token in {m,o,p}, third token in {x,o,z,...}, and for L=4 a fourth token in {x,o,z,r,e}. The strongest examples look like l m o x <DEL> [l] and m o x <DEL> [m]. Activation is highest when the second token is m/o and the next tokens are o/x; I did not test this further. It does not fire in the original phase (a few weak exceptions at t=4..6), on the delimiter itself, at later copy steps, or in long sequences. Acts like a lookup over specific short-sequence contents, so precision and recall are only moderate.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 39 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & out_tok=m (+2.24), orig1=m (+1.96), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=l (+1.91), prev2_tok=x (+1.88), orig0=m (+1.86), in_tok=z (+1.78). Lower it: in_count=1 (-0.94), in_first=1 (-0.89), n_digits=1 (-0.83), prev_tok=<DEL> (-0.29).
